title: The Moonsnag
pitch: The wood has one hole in its roof: the Moonsnag, a lightning-split dead giant whose hollow is the only place the real moon reaches the floor. Every moth Wing frees flies there and settles on its moonlit inner walls to wait for her. She lands in it at minute 3 and comes back to it four times, and it is never the same place twice. Each time the firefly has hung more of its lights under the moon hole, a chandelier that becomes a false moon. Her own moths drift up off the walls toward it, and an orb-weaver strings its web wider beneath it. Two spokes open at once and she picks the order. The Lampwalk to the east is warm and fast: fling chains, hawkers, and glide at the end. The Burrows to the west are dark and tight: beetle fights, the old burrback, a floor that breaks, the black roots, and claws in the moonlight under the hub. Each spoke ends with a shortcut that brings her back into the hub from a new direction, and her new ability opens a new pocket of it. With both abilities she climbs out over the canopy through the Silk Loft, looks down through the web at her moths caught in the false moon, and drops through. The hub becomes the boss arena, and the last fling of the fight carries her out through the moon hole with every moth she freed. It is fun because the centre is always changing and always meaning something, and because every spoke is dense and has a feeling of its own. Every way back feels like cracking the place open.
throughline: Wing wants out of the wood after the swarm, through the one hole in its roof, and to take every moth she frees with her before the false moon the firefly is hanging there draws them into the spider's web.

regions.name: The Hatching Branch
regions.note: Split cocoons, Tatter, the swarm streaming east past the moon. Control in 8 s. Under the branch, out of reach, hangs a moon-drop in a knot (the thorn chimney's prize, seen at second 10).

regions.name: The Fallen Limb
regions.note: The chase along a fallen limb after the swarm, then the vista from the limb's broken end: the swarm breaking up over the valley's lamps far east, and across the gap the Moonsnag's crown, a ring of moonlight in a roof of leaves. The title. Leaves to cut along the run, two wicks with stragglers to snuff on the way.

regions.name: The Thorn Chimney
regions.note: Optional and hard, with no enemies. A thorn-lined shaft from the Burrows' west end up to the hatching branch: kick, kick, a fling off a wick between the faces, a glide through a thorn gap, kick again. Three screens, each a checkpoint, and embers relight on a miss. At the top: the moon-drop under the branch. Seen from the Burrows from the first pass, with a thin moon shaft at its top.

regions.name: The Fern Slope
regions.note: The first fling: one wick over a gap (time slows, aim, launch, the flame snuffs behind her, moths burst out). Then a two-wick chain over thorns, a juvenile beetle on a landing, fern curtains to hack, and a dark hollow to the left with the first firefly sign (the wrong way pays). The slope ends on the hub's high west ledge, looking down into the Moonsnag. Climbing back up needs claws.

regions.name: The Moonsnag (the hub)
regions.note: One tall room, floor to moon hole: a moon patch on a root boss in the moon's pool, Tatter, the floor crack breathing cold air, the hollow walls (they slide before claws), the east arch (warm glow) and the west door (dark, beetle clicks). It changes on every visit. Visit 1: the firefly hangs the first light under the hole and darts out. Visit 2: her freed moths line the walls, three lights hang now with first silk under them, a dangler has moved in over the west door, and her new ability opens a pocket (glide: the upper west niche; claws: the split above the east window). Visit 3: five lights and a full web over the hole, her moths being drawn up off the walls, the moonlight on the floor cut into a web's shadow. Visit 4: the boss arena. After: dark, the web gone, the moon full on the floor, Gust's thorn niche to open.

regions.name: The Moon Hole
regions.note: The broken rim of the snag above the canopy. First seen from above at the end of the Silk Loft: through the web, the false moon, her moths circling it, the Weaver at its heart. She cuts the anchor thread and drops. After the boss: the moths lift out past her, the firefly darts in and relights one wick behind a thorn band on the rim, and the moonlight on the rim gives Gust. The way out runs east along the canopy.

regions.name: The Silk Loft
regions.note: The canopy's underside, strung with old webs that glint in the moonlight. Needs claws to get in and glide to cross. Danglers drop over the only standing spots, orb webs hang across glide lines (touching one brings its weaver), and wicks hang in the silk so that a fling chain through the web is the fast line and cutting a doorway is the slow one. It is the web gauntlet before the boss. A dark under-ledge holds a firefly sign: a half-strung row of glow-caps.

regions.name: The Firefly's Cache
regions.note: A hidden hollow above the glade, full of the firefly's unfinished work: glow-caps strung but never hung, a ring of lights in its flash rhythm, a lamp shaped like a firefly. It is a fling playground with no thorns, pure flow, and at the top is a moon-drop.

regions.name: The High Bough
regions.note: The lock room for glide: the only way out of the glade is a bough running west, high over the Lampwalk, with the Moonsnag ahead the whole way. Glide gaps, one with a hawker hunting a wick in the middle, a wick to fling off into a longer glide, and moths flying ahead to the snag. It ends in a long glide in through the hub's east window: the first shortcut, and visit 2 begins from above.

regions.name: The Fern Glade
regions.note: A moonlit hollow at the Lampwalk's end. Silence after the lit run. She basks: glide. Under the lip, a wick in an alcove. Overhead, high in the ferns, one flame hangs out of line with everything else: the honest tell for the cache.

regions.name: The Lampwalk
regions.note: The firefly's first strung road: a ravine east of the hub crossed on lamps. Fling chains over thorn floors, two hawkers hunting the air between flames, a beetle on the landing in each pool of light. Leaves and bark to cut and stragglers at every lamp: 2 to 3 things in reach all the way. A dark root ledge under the lamps is the slow, safe way. A bark floor between two lamps (dead moths fall through it and vanish) drops to a sunk pool: the drowned-roots stub and a moonlit hollow (long breath: the fling's slow time lasts longer).

regions.name: The Burrows
regions.note: Beetle galleries under fallen logs west of the hub: close, dark, mostly a fight. Juveniles, two adult beetles under low wicks (snuff and they sleep, or fight in the light), bark doors and bark floors to cut (each cut bounces her: the pogo learnt where a miss is free), seed pods to burst. A root window shows a hill that breathes: the old burrback asleep. The chimney's thorns climb into the dark at the west end.

regions.name: The Old Den
regions.note: The breathing hill wakes: the old burrback on a floor of moth wings. Ram, brace (only the pogo hurts it then), stomp. Its last stomp breaks the den floor, and she falls with it into the dark below (False Knight's floor). Moon patch at the door.

regions.name: The Black Roots
regions.note: Silent and black, no lamps and no music at first: dread. Then small lit pockets with danglers over the landings, the drowned-roots stub (a seeping root wall), and, under the hub, the moon column falling through the floor crack. Claws in that light. The climb-out goes straight up the column and breaks the crack's bark plug from below into the hub: the second shortcut, and Tatter goes through.

landmarks.name: The false moon (the firefly's chandelier), bigger each visit
The valley's lamps and the broken swarm (far east)
The breathing hill (the old burrback asleep)
The moon column through the floor crack

secrets.name: The moth-stone (the map)
secrets.tell: On visit 2 her freed moths settle on every wall of the hub except one low patch west of the patch: air moves behind it. The bark there takes cuts like the Burrows' doors.

secrets.name: The firefly's cache (a moon-drop)
secrets.tell: One flame hangs high in the glade's ferns, out of line with every road. Nothing else points at it.

secrets.name: The thorn chimney's moon-drop
secrets.tell: Seen at second 10, hanging under the hatching branch out of reach. The thorn shaft is in plain view from the Burrows' west end, with a thin moon shaft at its top.

secrets.name: The sunk pool (long breath, the drowned-roots stub)
secrets.tell: On the Lampwalk, a dead moth drops from a lamp onto a patch of floor and falls through it.

secrets.name: The hub's thorn niche (Gust)
secrets.tell: A wick burns behind a thorn band high on the hollow's wall on every visit, unreachable by blade or fling. Gust is the first thing that can touch it, on the way back through.

boss.name: The Weaver under the false moon
boss.idea: Fought in the hub itself, the room she has crossed four times, so she knows every wall. The firefly's chandelier is the great lamp, five wicks strung around a heart in the orb web across the moon hole, with her own moths circling it. P1, the ring (fling): she chains between the five wicks, each launch snuffing the one she leaves and dropping its spoke of web, while the Weaver runs along the strands to wherever she touches; a wrong line lands her in silk. Freed moths spill down to the walls with each snuff. P2, the drops (claws and glide): the web falls in sections and the Weaver drops on telegraphed threads from knots in the hollow's walls, swinging across half the room; the safe side is always the far wall, so she kicks up the snag's walls (now hers) and glides across. P3, the floor (pogo): the Weaver lunges along the floor and lies winded belly-up; only a pogo on the abdomen lands. Three pogos and it flees up the walls. The heart sinks, unguarded, and her final fling off it snuffs it and launches her up through the moon hole as every moth lifts with her. It tests the area's three moves in order, keeps the Weaver Matt liked, and turns the hub's change into the fight.

minuteByMinute: 0–1: The hatch and the chase along the fallen limb after the swarm. Leaves to cut, two straggler wicks, the moon-drop out of reach under the branch.
1–2: The vista. The swarm breaks over the valley's lamps, the Moonsnag's ring of moonlight is across the gap, and the title shows. Drop to the Fern Slope.
2–3: The first fling and a two-wick chain, a juvenile beetle on a landing, fern to hack, and the dark hollow to the left with a firefly sign.
3–4: The high ledge, then the hub. The patch and Tatter. The firefly hangs the first false light under the moon hole and leaves. Two doors: warm east, dark west.
4–6: The Lampwalk at full speed: chains over thorns, two hawkers between the flames, beetles in each pool. The sunk pool under a bark floor for those who watch the dead moths.
6–7: The Fern Glade: silence and glide. A flame out of line overhead (the cache). The only way out is up and a glide.
7–8: The High Bough: glide gaps west with the Moonsnag ahead, then a long glide in through the hub's east window.

8–9: Hub visit 2. Her moths line the walls, three false lights hang under the hole with first silk, a dangler hangs over the west door, and glide opens the upper west niche. One wall stays empty of moths (the moth-stone).

9–11: The Burrows: close fights with juveniles and beetles, wicks to snuff so they sleep, bark doors and floors to bounce through. The breathing hill through a root window. The thorn chimney glimpsed.
11–13: The Old Den. The old burrback's ram, brace and stomp; its last stomp breaks the floor and she falls into the black.
13–14: The Black Roots: a quiet minute of dread, then two lit landings with danglers, the drowned-roots stub, and the moon column under the hub.
14–15: Claws in the moon column, up through the crack. Hub visit 3: five lights, a full web, her moths being drawn up off the walls. The stakes are visible.
15–18: Up the split into the Silk Loft, the web gauntlet: danglers, orb webs across the glide lines, a fling chain through the silk or a doorway cut.
18–19: Round to the rim. Through the web, the false moon, her moths and the Weaver. Cut the thread and drop.
19–22: The Weaver in the hub: the ring by fling, the drops by claws and glide, the floor by pogo. The last fling launches her up through the moon hole as the moths lift.

22–24: On the rim the firefly relights one wick behind thorns, and the moonlight gives Gust: blow it out. Tatter climbs the fallen thread. East along the canopy. Optional: back down to Gust the hub's thorn niche, the chimney, the cache.
